lore.Noctis City: Deep in the Noctis Labyrinthus, shielded from cosmic rays by kilometre-high canyon walls, the first settlers found the perfect spot for a city.
lore.Tharsis Tholus: An old shield volcano with a caved-in summit. Its lava tubes were the first shelters of the Tharsis survey crews, and they still hum with ventilation fans.
lore.Ascraeus Mons: The northernmost of the three Tharsis giants, 18 km high. Its summit caldera is where the first orbital elevator was surveyed and abandoned.
lore.Pavonis Mons: Sitting almost exactly on the equator, the "Peacock Mountain" is the natural anchor for a space elevator; the survey beacons on its flank still blink.
lore.Arsia Mons: The southern Tharsis volcano, wrapped in morning cloud banks. Its caldera shelters the oldest ice deposits in the region, fought over since the first water rights charter.
lore.Ganymede Colony: Jupiter's largest moon, bigger than Mercury. The colony sits in the bright grooved terrain, trading water ice and patience with the inner system.
lore.Phobos Space Haven: The inner moon of Mars, skimming 6,000 km above the surface. Its hollowed-out Stickney crater became the busiest dock between Mars and the belt.
lore.Elysium Mons: The great volcano of the east, 12 km high and quiet for a few million years. Surveyors swear the summit is warmer than it should be; the geothermal consortium politely declines to comment.
lore.Hecates Tholus: Named for the goddess of crossroads and the night. Its flanks are carved by old glaciers, and the ice-miners who work them leave a lantern burning at the caldera rim for luck.
lore.Olympus Mons: The tallest volcano in the solar system: 22 km high and as wide as France. From the summit the horizon is so far away you cannot tell you are on a mountain at all. The view is still worth the three-week hike.
lore.South Pole: Layer upon layer of water ice under a seasonal cap of dry ice. Every spring the CO₂ sublimates in dark geysers that the locals call "spiders" and the tourists pay good money to watch.
lore.Alba Mons: The broadest volcano on Mars, spreading over 1,000 km yet barely 7 km tall. A mountain you can walk up without noticing, which the Alba Hill-Walkers’ Society counts as a feature.
lore.Uranius Tholus: A small, steep shield volcano sitting in the lee of its big brother Uranius Mons. The first automated weather station on the northern plains was bolted to its summit and still files a forecast every hour: dusty.
lore.Viking 1: The landing site of Viking 1, the first craft to work on the surface of Mars (1976). The lander is fenced off as a heritage site, and every new colonist is expected to leave one pebble at the gate.
lore.Viking 2: Where Viking 2 touched down on Utopia Planitia in 1976 and photographed frost on the rocks. The settlement grew up around the lander, and the frost is now celebrated every winter with a festival of very cold soup.
lore.North Pole: A cap of water ice nearly 3 km thick, streaked by spiral canyons carved by the wind. The ocean engineers call it "the reservoir", and they mean it.

help.title: How to play here
help.globe:
Globe
Drag to rotate · wheel / pinch to zoom · two-finger or right-drag to pan · double-click (or H) to recentre.
help.turn:
Your turn
Glowing cards in your hand are playable — click one to read it and play it. Standard projects, card actions, milestones and awards are on the right.
help.tiles:
Placing tiles
Candidate hexes glow gold. Hover to preview the tile and see what the space gives you.
help.undo:
Undo
Undo anything until a card is revealed. When your turn ends you get Confirm turn — nothing reaches TFMBot until you confirm. Ctrl+Z undo · Enter confirm · Esc cancel.
help.opp:
Opponent
Hover (or tap) a player board to see their tableau. The feed on the left shows each TFMBot move and what else it considered; the top bar shows its estimate of your win chance.
help.tracks:
Tracks
Temperature: heat-production bonuses at −24 and −20, an ocean at 0 °C. Oxygen: +1 temperature at 8%. Oceans: 9 slots.
help.hint:
💡 Hint
Asks TFMBot what it would play in your position, with the search share of its top options.
boot.msgs: Counting craters (lost count, starting again)…

Shuffling the deck (no peeking)…
Filling the ocean tiles with actual water…
Convincing lichen to grow…
Planting the first greenery (it’s very small)…
Feeding the Tardigrades…
Herding Martian microbes…
Plotting asteroid trajectories (mostly harmless)…
Looking for water on Mars (found some!)…
Counting megacredits twice, just to be sure…
Asking the value network how it feels…
Pruning the search tree (it was getting bushy)…
Reminding Helion that heat is money…
Getting United Nations Mars Initiative to agree on something…
Coaxing the first rain out of the sky…
Arguing about who places the first ocean…
Parking comets in a holding pattern…

Waving at Jupiter…
Measuring out exactly 9 oceans…
Finding room for one more greenery…

Almost there — the bot is stretching…

Loading the first shuttle with seeds and optimism…
Measuring Mars for a new atmosphere (size: thin)…
Teaching the bot the word “probably”…

Politely declining the Hired Raiders’ business card…
Rehearsing “I was going to take that milestone”…
Arranging the forests into a smiley face (visible from orbit)…
Offering the Fish their first ocean…
Convincing the Birds that oxygen is coming…
Updating the “days since last asteroid” sign: 0…
Reserving a window seat on the next shuttle…
Consulting the ancient Martian scrolls (the rulebook)…
